added_failures_note: The reviewed run's baseline_suite at 3aec564ad491f6d9d6dde4606786f2a68bc78231 and after_suite at 8d82950debd6fd48aa8f9f3756be2b2be2dbe283 both completed with one pass, EXIT=0, and no failure IDs; matched station logs each record 12 passes and no failure IDs.

assertion_analysis.fails_if: the station never requests the first sweep
the second requested sweep starts before the active one is released
a sweep thread remains alive after release
the pending request is dropped or replayed more than once
a review is dispatched during the first pass before the source is delivered
the review dispatcher does not store a dispatched status on the source pointer
the recovery report omits the dispatched review run id; its expected id is read from another production receipt and both could be wrong together
the dispatched review run pointer is absent or has the wrong role
the repair path does not record a resumed status
the repair path records no round id
the repair advice omits the independently supplied blocking finding
the review and repair paths together invoke the launcher fewer or more than twice
the first sweep begins before its request or after the second request
the second sweep begins before the first finishes or the second request arrives after the first finishes
the second sweep finish timestamp precedes its start timestamp

0.reason: the station never recorded per-session sweep request or start stamps, so the historical instance's timing cannot be recovered; the worker states the bounds that its transitions give and records exact request, start and finish stamps in a controlled replay; the done-when's demand for historical stamps was the coordinator's error

findings.text: blocking: the live incident's sweep request and start times were never retained, so the controlled replay cannot supply the historical live-session timing the plan's done_when explicitly requires.

blocking: the unchanged-scheduler negative control fails on the number of sweep calls before checking review_dispatch or repair_dispatch, so its recorded failure does not show both required duties absent.
